# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ -  The prices of all of the four main precious metals rebounded at the end of April after declining for some time. However, the short period of positivity could not be sustained and the Dollar firmed on a perceived lack of action by the Federal Reserve and growing concerns over the outlook for Europe as elections in France and Greece featured ever more often in the news. As a result, the price of each of the metals fell back in early May with little investor interest evident.  On COMEX/NYMEX all four precious metals saw an increase in net speculative long positioning in the final week of April. However, total investor exposure remains relatively low, suggesting that confidence is rather fragile.  In the precious metal ETFs, gold and platinum saw selling pressure while silver finally saw some light buying after a spell of selling pressure in recent weeks. Investors continued to show their interest in palladium over the longer term by adding to their ETF holdings yet again. Whether ETF buying can really be considered fundamental demand or not is not entirely clear but the net purchasing of 323,000 ounces of palladium in only four months does clearly have the potential to impact market dynamics. Likewise, the buying of over 13,000 ounces of rhodium through the rhodium ETF is quietly eroding some of the market surplus in that metal. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **08 May 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **08 May 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 1 May 2012; ETF data to 4 May 2012.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

On the 25th of April, the Federal Reserve declined to show its hand over the possibility of further quantitative easing. The Dollar weakened nonetheless, allowing the precious metals to gain some ground in price terms. A touch of stimulus from the Bank of Japan on the 27th added a little energy to prices and helped gold move higher to a peak of $1,665 on the 27th. The following week was more difficult though: the Chinese and Japanese markets were shut for part of the week for Golden Week/National Day holidays and buying interest was thin. Rumours of central bank selling weighed on gold and sell stops were triggered, sending gold down briefly to $1,653 on the 30th before rebounding. In the following days, poor European economic data and worries over the outcomes of the French and Greek elections sapped the market’s energy: the Dollar firmed against the Euro and precious metal prices retreated, with gold tumbling to $1,645 on the 4th of May before lurching below $1,630 today. -  After the previous week’s liquidation, net long speculative gold positions on COMEX rebounded, rising by 1.3 million ounces to a still meagre 18.7 million ounces. Open interest increased as fresh long positions were opened. Short positioning declined a little too, suggesting that speculators may see support for the gold price at or above $1,600. If prices start to rise or European concerns become more of an issue, there is plenty of room for long positioning to increase. -  For six of the last seven weeks, gold ETF holdings have declined even as concerns over Europe intensify. In the final week of April, investors sold a net287,000 ounces, taking holdings back below 70 million ounces for the first time since late January with most of the selling from the GLD/SPDR fund. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — May 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

-  Having settled close to $31.50 in mid-April, the silver price has made a determined move lower, finding support around $31 in late April before falling through $30 an ounce in early May to today’s fix of $29.58. Concern over European debt and European politics was negative for all of the precious metals and gold fell back under this pressure. However, poor German purchasing manager index data weighed more on the more industrial metals. The gold:silver ratio has moved from a low of 48.5:1 at the end of February to its current 55:1, demonstrating the lack of appetite for owning this riskier metal. -  Open interest in silver on COMEX declined by ten per cent in the final week of April. The net impact was a 7.2 million ounce increase in net long speculator positioning to a total of 133 million ounces. This does not, though, alter the picture of limited interest in silver at the moment from some industrial users and many speculators: positioning is still close to its lows for the year so far and ove

r 200 million ounces lower than its late October 2010 highs. -  As we commented last week, the heavy ETF selling previously seen was declining in strength and investors actually bought a net 976,000 ounces in the week to the 4th of May. Total holdings now stand at 455 million ounces. However, most of the buying was seen in the iShares fund with most of the other funds which we monitor reporting net outflows of metal. Investor views have evidently not become universally positive towards silver yet. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **08 May 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 1 May 2012; ETF data to 4 May 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

-  As with silver, platinum followed gold’s lead in price terms, firming at the end of April as the US Dollar weakened and softening as the Dollar firmed in early April. However, with the European economic climate looking worse by the week, there was little appetite shown by buyers of platinum, allowing gold to increase its premium over the traditionally higher value platinum. From the 25th of April to the end of the month, platinum rallied from $1,550 (on the 25th) to end the month at $1,570. The following week was always likely to be problematic for platinum with the Chinese and Japanese buyers largely absent. When the Dollar started to firm as European politics showed its disorderly side, platinum slid lower, falling initially to $1,560 on the 2nd before crashing to $1,535 on the 3

rd as the ECB declined to cut interest rates. The decline was not over though, with platinum hitting $1,512 on the 7th after Francois Hollande’s election in France worried the markets. It is now trading a little higher at roughly $1,525. -  Following eight successive weeks of bearish speculator activity, the final week of May finally saw platinum positioning on NYMEX rise by 102,000 ounces to just below one million ounces as investors opened new long positions in response to the “low” price. To illustrate the lack of investor interest, positioning has only been below this level for four weeks since the start of 2011. We expect the next commitment of traders report to show a further decrease in investor exposure. TOCOM positioning changed little. -  The slow selling in the platinum ETFs continued up to the 4th of May with a further 2,300 ounces sold from a mixture of funds. Although only 42,000 ounces have been sold since the 9th of March (with positioning falling from 1.515 million ounces to 1.473 million ounces during this period), the fact that the price decline has not generated more buying interest is a bearish sign. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **08 May 2012** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 1 May 2012; ETF data to 4 May 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

-  Palladium followed the other precious metals over the end of April and the start of May with currency movements and attitudes to risk dominating over

any fundamental issues. ETF investing and a light rebound in futures positioning provided the spur to drive palladium to a high of $685 on the 1st of May with $700 the clear short term target. Unfortunately, the growing expectation of a socialist win in the French elections and the upcoming Greek vote both placed pressure on the Euro. With weak economic data emerging too, the Euro weakened to a multi-month low and palladium slid lower, almost in a straight line, falling through $670 on the 2nd and $660 on the 4th. It is currently trading close to $640 and it will be interesting to see whether investors’ ardour has withstood this price weakness. 

-  Despite falling prices, some positive momentum has built in the palladium futures market with the last three weeks showing a continual improvement in sentiment. Net long positioning increased by 136,000 ounces in the final week of May, rising to 768,000 ounces as short positions were closed and fresh long contracts were opened. It would, though, be premature to see this as a bullish move: positioning remains low by historical standards and last week’s price weakness may have tested the resolve of some investors. 



-  In contrast to platinum, palladium ETF holdings increased once again in the week to the 4th of May, with a net 26,600 ounces purchased. So far this year, they have climbed from 1.736 to 2.059 million ounces, although they are still some 300,000 ounces below their record length. In only two weeks so far this year has there been net selling of ETF palladium. While futures investors are becoming a little more interested in the metal, ETF investors seem to have their eyes on the potential for longer term price appreciation.
